result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers say the designer is partly right, explain the physical limits of thread and pixels, and recommend a small set of simplified versions rather than a rebrand. B covers more of the causes, adding low contrast, gradients and fabric pile. It also gives more practical help: a digitizing cost, a chest-logo size and a ready-made request for the designer. A has the clearer quick test (solid black on white at 16 and 32px) but is a little thinner on causes. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers say the designer is partly right, blame the detailed logo for the failures, and suggest a few practical versions instead of a rebrand. B does slightly better: it links each cause directly to each failure, such as narrow gaps closing up and the tagline falling below the minimum letter height. It also gives a clear quick test (solid black on white at 16 and 32px) and lists exactly three versions. A covers gradients and contrast a bit more fully, but its test advice is thinner.
